title: [BUG] InMemoryKeyValueStorage.load() becomes extremely slow with large datasets
body: ### Required prerequisites - [x] I have read the documentation . - [x] I have searched the [Issue Tracker](https://github.com/camel-ai/camel/issues) and [Discussions](https://github.com/camel-ai/camel/discussions) that this hasn't already been reported. (+1 or comment there if it has.) - [ ] Consider asking first in a [Discussion](https://github.com/camel-ai/camel/discussions/new). ### What version of camel are you using? 0.2.75 ### System information ``` >>> import sys, camel >>> print(sys.version, sys.platform) 3.11.8 (main, Jan 14 2025, 13:47:38) [Clang 15.0.0 (clang-1500.3.9.4)] darwin >>> print(camel.__version__) 0.2.76a4 >>> ``` ### Problem description The InMemoryKeyValueStorage.load() method uses deepcopy() to return a copy of all stored records, which becomes a significant performance bottleneck as the dataset grows larger. ### Reproducible example code The issue with workforce enable share_memory. The main culprit for high CPU usage is the _collect_shared_memory function

linked_prs.title: fix: duplicate records for share_memory
linked_prs.body:
## Description

Issue:

Fixes duplicate record accumulation in Workforce shared memory (issue #3185) 

 Changes
  - Add deduplication in Workforce layer (better separation of concerns)

  Implementation

Workforce - Added UUID tracking for shared memories
    - Added _shared_memory_uuids: Set[str] to track already-shared records
    - Modified _share_memory_with_agents() to filter duplicates before sharing
    - Prevents exponential growth: only shares NEW records, not re-shared ones

  Root Cause

  Workforce's _sync_shared_memory() collected ALL records (including already-shared ones) and re-shared them every cycle. Now tracks shared UUIDs to prevent re-sharing.
